narrative.northStar: Back to Level in the Rain
narrative.overview:
A mobile home sits crooked under a storm-slate sky, and a crew comes out anyway and puts it back to level. Every surface of the system is drawn from that one scene: wet slate for ground, rain-washed siding for the light bands, and a single yellow spirit level whose bubble is the whole story. The yellow is the crew's tool, so it marks the one thing to do on any screen and the moment something reads true.

The voice is a working crew talking on the phone: heavy, uppercase, short headings in the device's own system face, then plain sentence-case body copy at a comfortable phone size. Density is low and single-column on phones, with big touch targets (44px minimum, 56px for primary actions). Bands of slate and paper are joined by puddle-surface seams that keep moving, so the page itself is weather.

The hero is a living canvas scene, not a photo: the visitor drags the home back to level themselves, and the level bubble confirms it.
keyCharacteristics: Storm-slate ground with rain-washed paper bands; one yellow accent.
Heavy uppercase system type for headings; sentence-case body.
Flat UI chrome; depth comes from tonal bands and the painted scene.
Moving puddle-wave seams between bands; motion is weather, not decoration.

rules.name: The One Bubble Rule
rules.body: Level yellow is the only accent in the UI chrome, and it means "this is the action" or "this is true". At most one yellow-filled control per viewport cluster; everything else is slate, paper, or ink.

rules.name: The Water Belongs to the Form Rule
rules.body: Rain blue is never a button fill or a headline color. It appears on input focus/hover and on the seams' water line, nowhere else.

rules.name: The Yellow-Off-Paper Rule
rules.body: Level yellow never sits as text on the paper band; use the paper-safe level there.

rules.name: The Shout-Then-Talk Rule
rules.body: Headings are 900-weight uppercase with tight tracking; everything below a heading is sentence case. Never set body or button text in uppercase.

rules.name: The House Stack Rule
rules.body: The system stack is the only typeface. Do not import a webfont; weight (400/600/700/800/900) and case carry all hierarchy.

rules.name: The Phone-First Column Rule
rules.body: Compose for one column at 375px first; wide layouts only split heading from content, they never add new content.

rules.name: The Thumb Rule
rules.body: Every interactive element is at least 44px tall; primary actions are 56px.

rules.name: The Weather-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Controls never lift off the page with shadows; they sit in it. Recess with a lighter slate fill, emphasize with yellow, separate with hairlines.

rules.name: The One Radius Rule
rules.body: Controls use 12px; nothing else gets a corner value. No cards, no pills on buttons.

rules.name: The Water Line Rule
rules.body: Bands that change color between story chapters meet at a puddle seam, not a straight edge or a diagonal.

rules.name: The One Loop Rule
rules.body: All continuous motion shares one requestAnimationFrame loop, each piece pauses when offscreen, and every motion has a reduced-motion state that still shows the finished picture.

dos: **Do** keep level yellow for the single primary action, the true/level moment, and focus.
**Do** set headings in 900-weight uppercase system type with negative tracking, and everything else in sentence case.
**Do** join color bands with a moving puddle seam (48px, swell 3, ripple 1.5).
**Do** use the 12px radius and 2px strokes on every control, with 44px minimum and 56px primary touch targets.
**Do** recess inputs and chips with slate puddle fill and turn their stroke rain blue on hover and focus.
**Do** pause any animation offscreen and provide a static, complete reduced-motion state.
donts: **Don't** add a second accent to the UI chrome; red, green and blue in the hero scene are world objects (jack, vial, rain), not palette.
**Don't** put drop shadows or gradients on UI controls or bands; shading belongs only inside the painted scene.
**Don't** import a webfont or use a display face other than the system stack.
**Don't** box content in cards; use open lists with hairline rules.
**Don't** set level yellow as text on the paper band.
**Don't** use stock imagery or icon-font glyphs; imagery is the drawn scene (or the crew's own work), icons are inline stroked SVG.
